LoRaWAN.definition: LoRaWAN is a low-power wide-area networking protocol designed to connect battery-operated devices to the internet through public, private or community networks.
LoRaWAN.deploymentFit: It is intended for IoT deployments that exchange relatively small amounts of data and need wide-area or difficult indoor coverage.
LoRaWAN.advantage: The standard is designed around range, device power use, network capacity and deployment cost.
LoRaWAN.limitation: Confirm that a suitable LoRaWAN network and the correct regional configuration are available for your project.

LTE CAT 1.definition: LTE Cat 1 is a 4G LTE device category first defined in 3GPP Release 8 and used by some IoT products.
LTE CAT 1.deploymentFit: It suits projects evaluating LTE cellular connectivity for IoT deployments.
LTE CAT 1.advantage: It provides an LTE connectivity option for IoT devices.
LTE CAT 1.limitation: Confirm local operator service and model requirements before ordering.

guides.title: How to Choose a LoRaWAN Gateway
guides.question: Which LoRaWAN gateway should I choose?
guides.answerTemplate: Choose from {count} LoRaWAN gateways. Start with the deployment setting and required backhaul: indoor models include LPS8N, LPS8v2, MS48-LR and LG308N, while DLOS8N is the outdoor model. Then compare the exact gateway functions, interfaces, power details and ZAR price stated for the SKU.
considerations: Choose an indoor model when the deployment requires indoor gateway hardware; DLOS8N is the outdoor model in the exact product set.

Confirm the required IP backhaul. LPS8N, LPS8v2 and MS48-LR state Wi-Fi and Ethernet; LPS8N and LPS8v2 describe cellular as optional, while LG308N and DLOS8N state cellular connectivity in their product details.
Choose the function that matches the system: LPS8v2 includes local LoRaWAN and IoT server functions, while MS48-LR adds a Modbus gateway role and local server functions.
Check gateway management and deployment features where stated, including LPS8N web/SSH management, LPS8v2 remote management, and DLOS8N auto-provisioning and remote monitoring.
Confirm the regional LoRaWAN frequency configuration, supplied power requirement, package details and exact SKU before ordering.
guides.differenceSummary: Indoor and outdoor gateway options are available. LPS8N bridges LoRaWAN to IP through Wi-Fi or Ethernet, with an optional cellular version. LPS8v2 adds local LoRaWAN and IoT server functions and also describes optional 4G. MS48-LR combines gateway, local server and Modbus functions with optional 4G. LG308N is available with Wi-Fi, Ethernet and cellular backhaul, while DLOS8N is the outdoor model and has optional cellular failover alongside outdoor deployment features. For other models, check the exact product details.
decisionPath: Decide whether the gateway must be indoor or outdoor, then shortlist the models whose product details match that setting.
Select the required backhaul: Wi-Fi or Ethernet, with optional cellular where the exact model supports it and the deployment requires it.
Choose any local server, Modbus, management or outdoor feature only when the exact SKU states it.
Confirm regional frequency, power, package information and price for the exact SKU before ordering.

guides.title: Choosing IoT Connectivity for Devices and Gateways
guides.question: How should I choose IoT connectivity for a device or gateway?
guides.answerTemplate: Choose connectivity in three layers: the sensor or equipment interface, the device uplink, and the gateway backhaul. RS485 and Modbus describe local device communication, while LoRaWAN and LTE CAT 1 are connectivity options shown on different products. A LoRaWAN gateway can also need an IP backhaul path such as Wi-Fi, Ethernet or cellular where its exact product details state it.
considerations: Identify the local sensor or equipment interface first, such as RS485 or Modbus where it is explicitly required.
Choose the device uplink separately, using the exact SKU to confirm LoRaWAN or LTE CAT 1 where shown.
For a LoRaWAN deployment, confirm whether a suitable gateway and network are available at the intended site.
For a gateway, confirm the required upstream backhaul path, such as Wi-Fi, Ethernet or cellular, only where the exact gateway details state it.
Confirm the deployment site can support the selected network path before ordering.
guides.differenceSummary: RS485 and Modbus are not alternatives to LoRaWAN or cellular connectivity. RS485 is a physical communication interface, while Modbus is a protocol that can use an RS485 link. LoRaWAN and LTE CAT 1 describe different IoT connectivity options. Gateway backhaul is the upstream connection a LoRaWAN gateway uses to reach network services.
decisionPath: List the sensor or equipment interface that must be connected.
Choose a product whose exact details state that interface and the required IoT connectivity.
Decide whether the device connects through a LoRaWAN gateway or uses cellular connectivity directly where shown.
If using a gateway, confirm its stated backhaul option and the available network at the deployment site.
Use the exact SKU to confirm regional configuration, power and project-specific requirements before ordering.

sections.title: What are you actually choosing?
paragraphs: Start by separating three decisions. The local device interface is how a sensor or piece of equipment connects, such as RS485. The device uplink is how an IoT device sends data, such as LoRaWAN or LTE CAT 1 when the exact product details state it. Gateway backhaul is the upstream path a LoRaWAN gateway uses to reach network services.
Keeping these layers separate avoids treating an equipment interface, an IoT uplink and a gateway's own network connection as the same choice.

sections.title: When LoRaWAN makes sense
paragraphs: LoRaWAN is the IoT connectivity option shown across the site's LoRaWAN products. It is used for IoT deployments that exchange relatively small amounts of data and need wide-area or difficult indoor coverage. Confirm that a suitable LoRaWAN network and the correct regional configuration are available for the project.
A LoRaWAN device uses a suitable LoRaWAN gateway and network. The gateway may then use a separate backhaul connection, depending on its stated features and the deployment.

sections.title: When cellular connectivity makes sense
paragraphs: LTE CAT 1 is the cellular IoT connectivity option represented by the site's active connectivity page. Use it only where the exact product details state LTE CAT 1, and confirm supported mobile service at the intended deployment site.

NB-IoT and LTE-M are cellular IoT terms buyers may encounter, but they are not separate active connectivity groups on this site. Do not assume an LTE CAT 1 product supports either one. Confirm the exact SKU before selecting any cellular technology.

sections.title: Wi-Fi, Ethernet and gateway backhaul
paragraphs: Wi-Fi and Ethernet appear in the product details of selected LoRaWAN gateways as IP backhaul options. They describe how the gateway can connect upstream, not how every sensor communicates with the gateway.

Use Ethernet on a LoRaWAN gateway when the exact gateway states Ethernet and the site can provide that connection. Use Wi-Fi only where the exact gateway states Wi-Fi. Some gateway variants also state cellular backhaul; confirm the exact model and deployment requirements.

sections.title: RS485 and Modbus in an IoT deployment
paragraphs: RS485 is a physical communication interface. Modbus is a protocol that can use an RS485 link. Neither is the same as LoRaWAN or cellular connectivity.

An RS485 or Modbus device can form part of an IoT deployment when a selected node or gateway explicitly states the required interface and its onward connectivity. Check wiring, protocol and register requirements before choosing.

questions.question: What is the difference between LoRaWAN and NB-IoT?
questions.answer: They are different connectivity approaches. This site has active product sections for LoRaWAN and LTE CAT 1. NB-IoT is not an active connectivity group here, so confirm it only when an exact product states it.

questions.question: Is RS485 the same as LoRaWAN?
questions.answer: No. RS485 is a local physical communication interface. LoRaWAN is an IoT connectivity option. A selected node or gateway can connect those layers only when its exact product details state the required interface and connectivity.

questions.question: Does Modbus require a gateway?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. Modbus is a protocol, and whether a gateway is needed depends on the equipment and the required onward connection. Confirm the selected product's stated interface, protocol and connectivity.

questions.question: When would I use Ethernet on a LoRaWAN gateway?
questions.answer: Use Ethernet when the selected gateway states Ethernet as a backhaul option and the site can provide that connection. Ethernet is the gateway's upstream path, not a claim about every connected device.

questions.question: What is gateway backhaul?
questions.answer: Gateway backhaul is the upstream connection a LoRaWAN gateway uses to reach network services. On selected gateway models, the stated options can include Wi-Fi, Ethernet or cellular.

questions.question: Should I choose LoRaWAN or cellular IoT?
questions.answer: Start with the connectivity path the site can support, then compare only products whose exact details state the required option. For LoRaWAN, confirm a suitable network and gateway. For cellular options, confirm supported service at the deployment site.

guides.title: Compare DDS20, DDS45 and DDS75 Distance Sensors
guides.question: How do DDS20, DDS45 and DDS75 distance sensors differ?
guides.answerTemplate: DDS20, DDS45 and DDS75 are ultrasonic distance-sensing product lines. DDS20 is for non-contact liquid-level measurement through a container over 20mm to 2000mm. DDS45 and DDS75 measure distance to a flat object, with ranges of 30mm to 4500mm and 280mm to 7500mm respectively.
considerations: Choose DDS20 when the measurement is liquid level through a container without contacting the liquid.
Choose between DDS45 and DDS75 by the flat-object range and measurement angle required: 30mm to 4500mm at 60° for DDS45, or 280mm to 7500mm at 40° for DDS75.
Compare the connectivity shown for the exact SKU, including LoRaWAN and LTE CAT 1 variants.
For LB and LS variants, compare the exact power entry: 8500mAh for LB or solar panel plus 3000mAh Li-ion battery for LS.
Confirm the target or container arrangement, required range, regional connectivity variant, and exact SKU before ordering.
guides.differenceSummary: DDS20 measures liquid level through a container without contacting the liquid. DDS45 and DDS75 measure distance to a flat object. DDS45 covers the shorter 30mm to 4500mm range with a 60° angle, while DDS75 covers 280mm to 7500mm with a 40° angle. Connectivity and power options vary by exact SKU.
decisionPath: Identify whether the project measures liquid level through a container or distance to a flat object.
For flat-object measurement, compare the required range and angle against the DDS45 and DDS75 product details.
Select the exact connectivity and power variant, then confirm the full product details before ordering.
